title: CUDA issue when using ddp_notebook on Kaggle
author: Chilliwiddit

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body:
Hi @Chilliwiddit, when instantiating `Llama finetuner`, cuda is initialized in main process resulting in bad cuda fork.

Especially the line:

```python
class LlamaFineTuner(pl.LightningModule):
    def __init__(self):
        
        pl.seed_everything(42)

        super(LlamaFineTuner, self).__init__()
        print(f"Llama finetuner 1: {torch.cuda.is_initialized()=}")
        
        # this initializes cuda in main process resulting in error
        base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained(
            model_name,
            #device_map={"": 0},
            low_cpu_mem_usage=True,
            dtype=torch.float16
        )
```

I verified by this simply adding bunch of statements: `print(f"IDENTIFIER: {torch.cuda.is_initialized()=}")`.

kaggle: https://www.kaggle.com/code/deependujha/lightning-issue-21561-code

A side note, have you tried [lightning studios](https://lightning.ai/)? It gives you more control over the runtime environment and lets you scale from consumer GPUs (like T4) to A100, H100, B200, etc., and much more feature rich.

I don't have much experience with `AutoModelForCausalLM`, but will give it a shot quickly to suggest a fix.


Thanks.

comments.author: deependujha
comments.body: hi @Chilliwiddit, you just need to move model instantiation code inside `def configure_model(self):`. ```python class LlamaFineTuner(pl.LightningModule): def __init__(self): pl.seed_everything(42) super(LlamaFineTuner, self).__init__() def configure_model(self): # create all your layers here base_model = AutoModelForCausalLM.from_pretrained( model_name, #device_map={"": 0}, low_cpu_mem_usage=True, dtype=torch.float16 ) self.model = get_peft_model(base_model, lora_config) self.tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name) ... ``` It's given OOM on T4 2 & 4 gpus. On L4 with 2 gpus, it worked fine. https://lightning.ai/lightning-ai/oss-litgpt/studios/yearling-copper-xr62/code?source=copylink
